assessment.result: Availability is checked against the current copied stock before any mutation. With validated unique SKUs, every accepted deduction is affordable; rejected orders perform no deductions and still append an ordered False outcome. Later orders continue with current stock. Empty orders satisfy all() and succeed.

Stock is copied, nested orders are only read, counts stay integers and outcome flags are booleans. Both signatures and result shapes are preserved. Adapter and decoder are unchanged, so JSON validation still completes before reservation and no new validation policy is introduced.

Concrete assertions through both APIs cover a later-item shortage, isolated rejection including untouched stock, subsequent exact-stock success, depletion against remaining rather than initial stock, empty batches/orders, integer/boolean types and nested input preservation. The later-item shortage and isolated rejection cases would detect partial mutation; the depletion case would detect stale availability checks.

Invalid JSON/shapes, duplicate identifiers/SKUs, unknown SKUs and invalid quantities exercise the unchanged decoder. Mocking batch.reserve verifies invalid later orders prevent engine invocation. Six original tests remain intact.

Behavior and usage match REQUEST, preserve original history and keep work bounded to the in-memory utility. Pending code-review text records the author handoff; this report supplies the subsequent independent verdict without implying human acceptance.
